reasons: Lake identity records United States v. Grubbs as a U.S. Supreme Court case decided 2006-03-21, year 2006.
Lake citations match the asserted official citation, parallel citations, and vendor-neutral Lexis citation.
The opinion centrally concerns an anticipatory warrant issued on an affidavit showing future probable cause.
The opinion requires the supporting affidavit to give the magistrate enough information to evaluate both aspects of probable cause for a conditioned anticipatory warrant, supporting the home role.
residual_risks: The disclosed files do not define a formal threshold for the corpus label 'Key,' but the case directly addresses the home topic.

defect.evidence_quote:
Most anticipatory warrants subject their execution to
some condition precedent other than the mere passage of
time
defect.problem: The holding line is clipped with a literal ellipsis and overstates the definition by implying all anticipatory warrants take effect only upon a future triggering condition. The opinion defines anticipatory warrants by future probable cause and says most, not all, have a triggering condition other than time.
defect.proposed_fix: Replace with: Anticipatory warrants are not categorically unconstitutional; a conditioned anticipatory warrant is valid when the affidavit establishes probable cause that the triggering condition will occur and that evidence will be present if it does.

reasons: The core proposition that anticipatory warrants are not categorically unconstitutional is supported by the opinion.
The definitional parenthetical and unfinished ellipsis need tightening to avoid overbreadth.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Avoid using a literal ellipsis in the holding field; state the full rule.
